about.title: Highland Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: In 2025, six traffic deaths were recorded in Highland alongside 154 injury collisions on roads like Baseline Street, Victoria Avenue, SR-210, and 9th Street. When a family loses a loved one to a collision caused by someone else's negligence, California law allows certain surviving relatives to pursue a wrongful death claim. This is separate from any criminal case that may follow, and it exists specifically to address the financial and emotional toll left behind. Because Saturday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. see a noticeable rise in reported crashes locally, families in Highland sometimes find themselves facing this exact situation after a weekend outing turns tragic. LawProactive doesn't practice law - we simply connect grieving families with an independent attorney who can explain standing, deadlines, and what losses may be recoverable, so no one has to sort through this alone during an already difficult time.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Sooner Rather Than Later

items.title: Standing Is Limited by Law
items.desc: California restricts who may file - typically a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, with certain dependents or heirs eligible after. An attorney can clarify who in your family qualifies before any claim moves forward.

items.title: The Clock Is Shorter Than You'd Think
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, but that window shrinks significantly if a government entity was involved, such as a city road issue. Missing that deadline can close the door on recovery entirely.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Bills
items.desc: California law allows families to seek compensation for funeral costs and lost financial support, but also for the loss of love, companionship, and guidance - losses that are harder to quantify but still legally recognized.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in Highland?
items.answer: California law generally gives priority to a spouse, domestic partner, or children of the person who died. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may have standing. An independent attorney can review your family's situation and confirm eligibility.

items.question: Does the corridor where the crash happened on Baseline Street or SR-210 matter for the claim?
items.answer: The specific road matters mainly for gathering evidence, such as collision reports or witness accounts, not for determining legal standing. What matters most is establishing negligence and the losses your family experienced. Local corridors like these do see regular collision reporting, which can help build the factual record.

items.question: How long do we have to bring a wrongful death claim after losing a family member?
items.answer: Generally, California gives families two years from the date of death to file. That deadline is often much shorter if a government agency or public roadway defect was involved. Speaking with an attorney early helps make sure the deadline isn't missed.
